newsitem.title: CHINA: Meiling sees rise in first-half 1997 net.
newsitem.headline: Meiling sees rise in first-half 1997 net.

text.p: Hefei Meiling Co Ltd, one of China's top refrigerator makers, estimated a minimal rise in its net earnings in the first half of 1997 due to stronger sales, a company spokesman said on Monday.
Meiling sold more than 400,000 refrigerators in the first half of 1997, a marginal rise from the year-ago period, he told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
"Our earnings increased in line with sales," the official said but declined to give a figure.

Meiling, which listed 100 million hard currency B shares in Shenzhen last August, booked net profits of 79.8 million yuan on sales of 840.5 million yuan in January-June 1996 under Chinese accounting standards. No figures using international standards were given.
Meiling, which also produces washing machines, aimed to sell one million refrigerators this year, compared with 800,000 in 1996, he said.

Meiling expected to turn out 100,000 washing machines in 1997, the official said, adding that washing machines would continue to account for a relatively small amount of the firm's business over the next several years.
Meiling had a 75 percent interest in a washing machine venture in Hefei, capital of eastern Anhui province, with Italian appliance maker Merloni Elettrodomestici, he said.
Merloni held the remaining 25 percent in the 150-million-yuan venture, which started operation in April 1996, the official said.
Meiling planned a 2.22-for-10 rights offer to A share and state institutional share holders to raise 300 million yuan for an ozone-friendly refrigerator project, the company has said.

Meiling would complete the issue, priced at 4.80 yuan per rights share, next month before launching a similar rights offer to B share holders later this year, according to Meiling's prospectus made public last week.
